6ac3625864b002646ee89f1c.title: Smart Health Tracker & AI Diet Assistant
6ac3625864b002646ee89f1c.desc: A mobile-friendly web app where users log meals. Uses ML to estimate calories from food photos and generate tailored dietary plans.

riskReport.top_blocker: Insufficient ML expertise causing missed deadlines

risks.title: Pre‑trained model fails to meet calorie‑estimation accuracy requirements
risks.description: The MobileNetV2 model fine‑tuned on Food‑101 may produce >30% error on real‑world meals, making the core value proposition unreliable.
risks.mitigation: Within one week run a quick benchmark on 50 sample images, record MAE, and if error >20% replace the model with a publicly‑available calorie‑regression model (e.g., CalorieCam) or add a simple rule‑based fallback.

risks.title: Feature creep due to vague requirements
risks.description: Missing concrete definitions for authentication, diet‑plan generation, and UI flows can expand work beyond the 60‑day window.
risks.mitigation: Spend two days creating a Minimum Viable Product (MVP) backlog with user stories, acceptance criteria, and a fixed deadline for each; lock the backlog before any new feature is added.

risks.title: Dataset licensing or availability issues
risks.description: Relying on Food‑101 and TensorFlow Hub models assumes they remain freely downloadable; a change in licensing could halt development.
risks.mitigation: Download and archive the required dataset and model weights today, verify they are stored in the repo's data folder, and document the source and license in a README.

risks.title: Insufficient ML expertise causing missed deadlines
risks.description: Team members rate Python/ML at 3/5 and have no prior experience with image regression, risking prolonged debugging and integration time.
risks.mitigation: Allocate a 5‑day intensive learning sprint: each member completes a short TensorFlow/Keras tutorial, then pairs to implement a minimal inference pipeline using the pre‑trained model.

risks.title: DevOps / deployment bottleneck on cloud resources
risks.description: Deploying Flask + React on a free tier cloud (e.g., Heroku) may hit dyno limits, causing integration testing delays.
risks.mitigation: Within one week set up a Docker‑compose local environment that mirrors the production stack, and reserve a low‑cost VPS for final staging to avoid free‑tier throttling.

immediate_actions: Create a detailed MVP backlog with user stories, acceptance criteria, and fixed sprint dates (Day 1‑2).
Clone the Git repo, set up branch protection, CI pipeline, and download/archive the Food‑101 dataset and pre‑trained MobileNetV2 weights (Day 1).
Schedule a 5‑day ML crash‑course sprint: assign tutorials, set daily deliverables, and produce a working inference script by the end of the week (Day 1‑5).
